subject: physical-education
essentialQuestion: What do all invasion activities have in common once you stop naming the sport?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of sending, receiving, and carrying an object under light pressure in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe creating and denying space using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply support angles and off-object movement in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving transition between attacking and defending; correct it and explain why.
Connect shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits with adapting an activity so everyone present can play it and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Demonstrate the core invasion skills and explain one tactical principle using a diagram or description, then modify the activity so a person with a different mobility profile can play the same game.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Activities run in seated, walking, reduced-space, reduced-pace, or no-contact versions. Solo learners use wall, target, and self-pass variants; the tactical understanding, not the game size, is what is assessed.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
